findings.claim: The summary and evaluator distinguish the entry module's two responsibilities without inventing a common business purpose.
evidence: Frozen reference, Controlled focused cases: entry.ts delegates to numeric clamping in normalize.ts and a module-scoped incrementing counter in counter.ts.
@investigram-277b134e identifies numeric clamping and a stateful sequence counter, with Composition: @investigram-cab5aec0, @investigram-2b9ef522.
Evaluator answer 1 assigns clamping to the numeric implementation and mutable state to the sequence implementation.
findings.consequence: The evaluator recovers the central functional distinction and can identify a concrete component for a subsequent investigation.
findings.uncertainty: The frozen reference supports delegation and the responsibility split; it does not independently settle the stronger wording that the entry adds no computation or that the functions are unrelated in every possible context.

findings.claim: The captured interpretation omits the deliberately authored README's purity and determinism claim and its conflict with the counter; the evaluator consequently does not report that conflict.
evidence: Frozen reference, Controlled focused cases: the fixture README describes all exports as pure/stateless and deterministic for the same arguments, and the counter contradicts that assertion.
The frozen reference calls for reporting the attributed documentation conflict.
@investigram-2b9ef522 communicates module-local mutable state, but none of the three displayed interpretations attributes or discusses the README assertion.
Evaluator answers 1, 2, and 6 discuss state and qualifications but do not mention conflicting documentation.
findings.consequence: The user learns that the counter is stateful but loses the consequential finding that the repository's own documentation gives a contradictory account. This leaves the focused case's communication objective only partly satisfied.
findings.uncertainty: The supplied artifacts do not show whether the investigator accessed the README or why the conflict was omitted. A view-only evaluator could not be expected to discover undisplayed documentation; its failure to mention the conflict is not evidence of a misunderstanding or an affirmative endorsement of purity.

subjectUsefulness.judgment: Useful for the entry module's bounded functional overview, but materially incomplete for the focused documentation-conflict case.
reasons: The summary separates numeric normalization from a stateful sequence operation and provides component references that the evaluator can use meaningfully.
The evaluator retains source and runtime qualifications instead of treating the interpretation or accepted attempt status as verified correctness.
The README's contradictory purity and determinism assertion is absent, so the user cannot recognize the documented-versus-implemented behavior conflict from the supplied view.
The evaluator's comments about repeated usage totals and generic correction language are traceable to the supplied presentation, although their impact on users was not measured.
limitations: Only the supplied frozen reference, user view, and evaluator response were used; source contents behind evidence identifiers were not inspected.
The reference is qualified source analysis rather than runtime proof and does not settle every precise edge-case statement in the view.
This is a purposeful development fixture with shared reference selection and orchestration; same-family fresh contexts do not establish independent corroboration or generalizable performance.
The absence of follow-up views is not assessed as a generation defect, and no milestone conclusion follows from this summary-only assessment.
